question: Under perfect competition, a firm earns _________ profits in the long run.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Normal**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the long run, **all factors of production are variable**. Also, two of the assumptions of firms in perfect competition are free entry and exit, as well as perfect resource mobility.
 
• In the long run, firms making an abnormal profit will attract new firms, which will enter freely due to the **two assumptions already stated**.
 
• This would **increase the industry supply** (and shift the supply curve to the right) which will decrease the industry price. New firms will stop entering the market once existing firms make zero economic profit.
 
• The long run is a period of time which is sufficiently long to allow the firms to make **changes in all factors of production**. In the long run, all factors are variable, and none are fixed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Under perfect competition, price determination takes place at the level of industry while firm behaves as a price taker. It produces a quantity depending upon **its cost structure**.
 
• **There are two methods of finding the equilibrium of a firm**– TR-TC method and MR-MC method. Price determination in the industry takes place through price mechanism, i.e., through the interaction of demand and supply forces.
 
• In the long run under perfect competition, the firm earns **only normal profit**. As entry of a new firm reduces the abnormal profit. The long-run equilibrium occurs where demand intersects marginal cost and the minimum point of average cost.
 
• In economics, specifically **general equilibrium theory**, a perfect market, also known as an **atomistic market**, is defined by several idealizing conditions, collectively called **perfect competition**.
